paper.title_en: Resolving Galactic and Cluster Dynamics Without Dark Matter: Tsallis Entropy as the Unique Foundation of Emergent Gravity
paper.abstract_en: While modified entropy models-such as Barrow, Tsallis, Kaniadakis,Power-law, Logarithmic, and Rényi entropies-have been widely explored in cosmological contexts, their implications on galactic scales remain largely untested. These generalizations of the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy encode quantum gravitational, nonextensive, or fractal spacetime effects and can alter the gravitational entropy-area relation. In this paper, we demonstrate that the entropic force framework, when applied to galactic rotation curves and the baryonic mass of galaxy clusters, uniquely selects Tsallis entropy as the specific generalized entropy formulation. We then extend this Tsallis modified gravity to globular clusters to complete the structural hierarchy from galaxies to galaxy clusters to globular clusters and to investigate its behavior as a function of system scale. We will show that the nonextensive parameter exhibits no correlation with any of the macroscopic quantities characterizing gravitational systems, such as mass, radius, temperature, or density. Furthermore, it has previously been shown that entropy is not well-defined within the standard thermodynamic approach to gravity. The adoption of nonextensive statistics provides a foundation for entanglement, thereby enabling a consistent definition of entanglement entropy. We predict the existence of galaxy clusters with $δ= 1$ (i.e., clusters whose dynamics require no dark matter) analogous to $δ= 1$ systems already observed at galactic and globular cluster scales. This prediction provides a unique observational test to discriminate Tsallis gravity from $Λ$CDM and MOND. Therefore, for the entropic gravity paradigm to be consistent with observational data across all scales-from globular clusters to galaxies to galaxy clusters-it is inevitably required to be built upon \textit{Tsallis} entropy.

decision.selection_reason_zh: 论文提出Tsallis熵作为涌现引力唯一基础的独特观点，并预测无暗物质星系团的存在，具有理论深度和新颖性。
decision.title_zh: 无暗物质解释星系和星团动力学：Tsallis熵作为涌现引力的唯一基础
decision.abstract_zh: 虽然修正熵模型——如Barrow、Tsallis、Kaniadakis、幂律、对数和Rényi熵——已在宇宙学背景下被广泛探索，但它们在星系尺度上的影响在很大程度上仍未得到检验。这些对Bekenstein-Hawking熵的推广编码了量子引力、非广延或分形时空效应，并且可以改变引力熵-面积关系。在本文中，我们证明了当熵力框架应用于星系旋转曲线和星系团的重子质量时，唯一地选择了Tsallis熵作为特定的广义熵公式。然后，我们将这种Tsallis修正引力扩展到球状星团，以完成从星系到星系团到球状星团的结构层次，并研究其作为系统尺度函数的行为。我们将证明，非广延参数与表征引力系统的任何宏观量（如质量、半径、温度或密度）都没有相关性。此外，先前已经表明，在标准的引力热力学方法中，熵并不是良好定义的。采用非广延统计为纠缠提供了基础，从而能够一致地定义纠缠熵。我们预言存在δ=1的星系团（即其动力学不需要暗物质的星团），类似于已经在星系和球状星团尺度上观察到的δ=1系统。这一预言提供了一个独特的观测检验，以区分Tsallis引力与ΛCDM和MOND。因此，为了使熵引力范式在所有尺度上（从球状星团到星系到星系团）与观测数据一致，它必然需要建立在Tsallis熵的基础上。
